title: Climate-resilient water infrastructure finance
bottleneck: Adapting water systems to floods, droughts, and salinization needs trillions in investment, but the finance gap is starkest where need is greatest: utilities in developing countries cannot borrow affordably, climate risk makes projects unbankable by conventional metrics, and adaptation benefits — avoided disasters — do not generate revenue to repay loans. No financial instrument has cracked the problem of funding resilience whose payoff is something not happening.
why_it_blocks: Water system failures cascade into health crises, food insecurity, and conflict; underinvestment guarantees repeated disasters. The finance gap means adaptation is fastest where it is least needed.
current_state: Green bonds, resilience bonds, and blended finance pilots are testing new structures, and multilateral funds are growing. But flows remain an order of magnitude below estimated needs, and the fundamental bankability problem is unsolved.
